checks.explanation: Per-mile insurance pioneer Metromile did not build a dominant moat forcing incumbents to raise rates; instead it struggled as a standalone business and was acquired by Lemonade in 2022 in an all-stock deal, with Lemonade later retiring the Metromile brand entirely.
Both Pfizer/BioNTech and Moderna's mRNA COVID-19 vaccines received FDA Emergency Use Authorization in December 2020, with reported efficacy around 95%.

Actual US vaccine rollout badly missed this optimistic pace: by January 23, 2021, only about 41.4 million total doses had been distributed since mid-December (not 40 million in December alone), and only about 20.5 million had actually been administered.

sources.title: U.S. CDC says 41.4 million doses of COVID-19 vaccines distributed, 20.5 million administered

checks.explanation: The US did not reach 70% immunization by May 2021; even the more modest goal of 70% of adults with at least one dose (announced by the Biden administration for July 4, 2021) was narrowly missed until early August 2021.

The US was not in a comfortable pandemic position within a couple months; January 2021 was instead the deadliest month of the pandemic to that point, with case counts and deaths far exceeding prior peaks, before vaccination had scaled meaningfully.
By summer 2021, in-person conferences and international leisure travel (including to Europe) had resumed meaningfully in the US, ahead of the later Delta-wave setbacks.

No pandemic of comparable scale to COVID-19 has emerged since 2020 to meaningfully test a 'Warp Speed 2.0' response, so this speculative claim about response speed for a future pandemic remains untested.

Moderna is widely reported to have designed its COVID-19 vaccine candidate sequence within about two days of receiving the SARS-CoV-2 genome, with the remaining delay to deployment coming from manufacturing scale-up, clinical trials, and regulatory review, closely matching this prediction.
The UK's first COVID-19 human challenge trial dosing did not begin in January 2021; ethical approval came on February 16-17, 2021, and the first phase of dosing actually launched in April 2021.

sources.title: Human challenge trial launches to study immune response to COVID-19

checks.explanation: Income share agreement (ISA)-based trade schools did not proliferate to replace university trade training; the ISA model instead contracted, with high-profile players like Lambda School (rebranded BloomTech) facing regulatory scrutiny and enforcement action rather than expanding into a dominant alternative to college.
The US economy rebounded strongly in 2021, with real GDP growth of roughly 5.9%, one of the strongest annual growth rates in decades, consistent with the vaccine-driven recovery predicted here.
2021 was significantly better than 2020 economically and in terms of pandemic conditions overall, once vaccines scaled through the year, matching this prediction.

Falling wind and solar costs did not render oil extraction broadly economically infeasible within 3-4 years; US oil production instead hit record highs in 2023-2024, and oil remained highly profitable for producers throughout this window.

The predicted 15-year window runs through roughly 2035, which has not yet arrived as of 2026; Dwayne Johnson has not run for president and has publicly downplayed the idea, but the window for this prediction to resolve is not yet closed.

No explicit timeframe was given, and while Iran has experienced significant internal unrest since 2020 (notably the 2022 Mahsa Amini protests) and regional conflict involving Israel, it has not descended into a full-scale civil war as of 2026, leaving this open-ended prediction neither clearly confirmed nor closed off.
